purpose: Original practice candidates from newly discovered official DTR teaching activity, not yet in questions.js

items.stem: A chatbot produces different employer shortlists in two fresh chats using the same prompt. What does this establish?
choices: One shortlist must be deliberately fraudulent
The prompt is invalid because it was written in English
The output exhibits run-to-run variability; a single shortlist cannot establish stable visibility
The model provider necessarily changed ownership
items.explanation: Repeated identical conditions can expose variation in model outputs; differences alone do not establish the underlying cause.
items.teaching_locator: Step 1: repeat each variant in two separate chats
items.independent_locator: A statistical framework for evaluating the repeatability and reproducibility of large language models, abstract

items.stem: An LLM visibility audit changes both the applicant's city and career stage between two prompts. What is the main interpretive problem?
choices: It proves that city alone caused any change
The effects of city and career stage cannot be isolated from that comparison
The audit no longer concerns platform power
items.explanation: Changing multiple factors together confounds attribution; one-factor-at-a-time comparisons help isolate a difference but cannot identify interactions or eliminate output variability.
items.teaching_locator: Step 1 Variant E: change only one profile element
items.independent_locator: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, section 5.2.1.2, one factor at a time and interaction limitations
